newsitem.title: UK: MOTOR RACING-TYRRELL SAYS IT WILL BE ALMOST IMPOSSIBLE TO RACE I.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-TYRRELL SAYS IT WILL BE ALMOST IMPOSSIBLE TO RACE I.

text.p: Veteran Formula One team boss Ken Tyrrell said on Tuesday that it may be impossible for his team to race in Italy next year in the light of the manslaughter charges brought against Frank Williams and five others following the death of Ayrton Senna in 1994.

"You have to say that it is difficult to understand how we can race in Italy if this is going to be the sort of situation after an accident," said 72-year-Tyrrell, who guided Jackie Stewart to world championship titles in 1971 and 1973.

"Motor racing is a dangerous sport. The drivers themselves know that and, although the loss of Ayrton was awful, and it is awful to lose any driver, I don't think we will be able to get insurance cover to prevent a similar situation (criminal charges)."
"We are talking about an accident that happened to one of the best prepared cars in the history of motor racing. If that has an accident for whatever reason...I don't see how any of us can be safe.
"I have no doubt that F1 teams will be getting together to decide what action to take. It is a matter of great concern because it could affect motor racing around the world."
Tyrrell's comments came a few days after another F1 team boss, Benetton's Flavio Briatore, said he would not race his cars in Italy if there were convictions.
"I would not risk bringing my team to a country that can convict you for an accident," he said. "Fatality is part of the game."

The five other men charged with manslaughter in connection with Senna's death during the 1994 San Marino Grand Prix are Patrick Head, Williams's technical director, Adrian Newey, Williams's chief designer, Roland Bruynseraede, the official race director, and Federico Bendinelli and Giorgio Poggi, officials representing the Imola circuit.
The first court hearing has been set for February 20, 1997, before a local judge in Imola.
